To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of an existing knowledge base in evaluating new facts can prevent simple but common inconsistencies; 2) the use of the same knowledge base in evaluating potentially inconsistent data can reveal facts that may require further evaluation; 3) the use of a knowledge base to evaluate new facts requires a mechanism for representing and maintaining knowledge base structure; and 4) the use of knowledge base contents to evaluate new facts can be automated to some degree, but requires user assistance to achieve high-quality results
(1) the use of existing knowledge can improve the consistency of the knowledge base, and (2) consistency enforcement can be used to identify potentially inconsistent data.
